Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's third quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust gross written premiums growth across our key lines of business, favorable trends in customer acquisition costs, disciplined combined ratio performance, and proactive capital deployment plans including acquisitions and innovative new products.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.82 per share, beating consensus estimates by 8%. Key drivers of our financial performance included double-digit gross written premium expansion, underwriting efficiencies, and strategic investments yielding high returns. Our combined ratio was 93.2% on a reported basis, or 91.8% excluding catastrophes—our best attritional quarter since 2019. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with approximately $4.2 billion in deployable capital, up 12% year-over-year, and a risk-based capital ratio of 620%, well above our internal target of 500%.

Let me start by diving into our top-line performance, specifically gross written premiums, or GWP, which grew 13.2% year-over-year on a reported basis, and 12.8% at constant exchange rates. This marks our strongest quarterly GWP growth in over five years, powered by disciplined pricing, improved rate adequacy, higher retention rates averaging 88.5% globally, and strong new business wins. Excluding the impact of our recent acquisition of a specialty portfolio, organic GWP growth was a solid 11.4%, highlighting the resilience of our core underwriting engine.

Breaking this down by line of business provides the best insight into our execution in a hardening market. Starting with property and casualty personal lines, we saw 9.7% growth to $2.8 billion. Homeowners led with 14.2% growth, capturing 8-10% rate increases on renewals in catastrophe-prone areas like Florida and California after the active Atlantic hurricane season, including events like Hurricane Idalia that tallied $3 billion in industry losses. Volume grew another 4%, driven by our Zenith HomeGuard bundled product with parametric triggers for wildfire and flood, lifting cross-sell penetration to 42% from 35% last year.

Auto grew 7.1%, moderated by softer commercial rates in non-fleet segments, but offset by telematics adoption now at 65% of U.S. policies through our ZenithDrive app. This usage-based approach cut loss trends by 2.5 points via superior risk selection, supporting 5% earned rate gains and 2.8% growth in policies in force. North America drove 75% of this segment's growth at 11.2%, while Europe grew 5.4% amid regulatory pressures from the EU's Sustainable Insurance Directive.

Commercial property and casualty shone with 11.5% growth to $3.1 billion, showing momentum across middle-market and large accounts. Workers' comp surged 13.8% on 7% pricing discipline and payroll recovery post-COVID, while general liability and umbrella grew 10.2% as supply chain inflation normalized claims severity. Strength came in construction and manufacturing, where our AI-driven predictive modeling with partners like Palantir boosted underwriting accuracy, achieving 92% retention and 15% higher average premium per risk.

APAC led regionally at 16.7%, with expansions in Australia and Southeast Asia layering cyber-physical endorsements amid geopolitical risks. North America added 12.4%, moderated by California wildfire reinsurance, and EMEA contributed 8.9% by optimizing our U.K. excess and surplus book.

Specialty lines accelerated 19.8% to $1.2 billion, leaning into high-margin areas. Cyber exploded 28.4%, riding a 35% industry-wide ransomware surge per our claims data, with 12-15% rate hikes and expanded capacity via our Lloyd's syndicate. D&O grew 16.2% on equity volatility and ESG litigation, akin to trends at Chubb and AIG. Marine and energy added 14.7%, boosted by LNG demand and Red Sea issues, with parametric hull coverage securing mandates from major shipping clients.

We've invested $150 million in tech this year, including blockchain for marine cargo and machine learning for cyber scoring, de-risking the book and increasing new business submissions 25%. APAC led at 25.3%, Europe at 18.1%, North America at 17.6%.

Life and health grew steadily 6.4% to $1.4 billion, from group health renewals at 7.2% amid 5.8% U.S. medical cost trends. Individual life was flat as we optimized by exiting low-margin universal life for hybrid critical illness products, with 90% retention via our digital health ecosystem and wearables.

Geographically, North America was 52% of GWP with 13.8% growth, fueled by P&C rate hardening and a $500 million M&A pipeline. EMEA grew 9.2%, navigating softer motor demand but gaining in specialties. APAC starred at 18.6%, scaling India and China ventures via bancassurance like Allianz's model, eyeing 20% CAGR through 2025.

Forward-looking, we guide 10-12% full-year organic GWP growth, with 6-8 points from pricing. Initiatives include embedded insurance APIs inspired by leading tech stacks, ESG-linked products for millennials, and reinsurance renewals locking favorable terms post-cat bond issuance, all supporting sub-95 combined ratios.

Shifting to combined ratio guidance, our north star for P&C underwriting discipline. Q3 was 93.2% reported, 91.8% ex-cat, reflecting 4% earned premium growth to $8.2 billion from mid-teens rates in personal auto and commercial multi-peril, offset by moderating cat losses from Hurricane Beryl's tail. Loss ratio was 66.4%, aided by $120 million favorable prior-year development in workers' comp and general liability as social inflation eased with verdict caps. Expense ratio steady at 26.8%, from $250 million annualized synergies of our 2023 Midwest Mutual acquisition.

For Q4 2024, we expect reported combined ratio of 94% to 96%, ex-cat 92% to 94%, implying a slight uptick from elevated cats modeled at $400-600 million from California wildfires and Southeast storms, in line with peers like Travelers and Chubb. Year-to-date cat load is 5.8 points, matching industry 6% per ISO, with our quota-share reinsurance capping net retention at 45% for peaks.

For full-year FY 2025, combined ratio guidance is 92% to 94%, ex-cat 91% to 93%, our strongest annual underwriting margin pre-COVID, targeting $1.2 billion P&C income. Drivers include: earned premium growth of 7-9%, with 5-7% organic rate in personal lines like 8% homeowners amid 12% YoY repair inflation per Xactimate, and 6% commercial with E&S share gains up 15% YoY. Telematics at 35% of auto policies delivers 200 bps loss improvement via ZenithEdge 2.0 AI pricing, segmenting risks 40% more granularly and cutting adverse selection 15%.

Loss ratio expected 65-67% reported, 64-66% ex-cat, with $400-500 million prior-year releases as bodily injury stabilizes, nuclear verdicts down 10% per Verisk. Auto physical damage inflation at 9% countered by 85% preferred repair networks and drone triage slashing cycle times 25%. Liability social inflation watched, but 20% umbrella attachment hikes effective.

Expense ratio 26-27%, down from 28% in 2022, via 72% straight-through claims processing rivaling benchmarks, saving $150 million yearly, and $100 million reallocated to gen-AI underwriting with Palantir for cat modeling amid 20% higher hurricane losses per RMS.

Regionally, U.S. P&C (75% premiums) at ex-cat 90-92%, strong Midwest agribusiness and Northeast habitational, cautious Florida and California. Europe (15%) 93-95% with softening D&O but German floods; Lloyd's cyber exclusions key. APAC like Australia motor (10% expansion) pulls to sub-92% ex-cat, offset Japan quakes via parametrics.

This embeds our Fortress Portfolio: exiting New York no-fault (20% non-renewals), doubling high-margin E&S/cyber with 25% attachment rises. Reinsurance flat at 2.8 loss ratio points via sidecars with Apollo and RenaissanceRe. Upside from telematics/GLMs; risks cat tails or 15% auto inflation, but $4.5 billion liquidity and 250% coverage resilient. This drives 12-15% ROE expansion without growth chasing.

Before questions, a word on customer acquisition cost trends, key to profitability. CAC—marketing, commissions, leads, onboarding per new policy—hit blended $285 in Q3, down 12% YoY from $325 and 5% sequentially from Q1's $300. This is peer-leading vs. Progressive/Travelers at $320-350 P&C, far below life peers over $800.

Quarterly: Q2 2023 $325; Q3 $310 (-5%); Q4 $295 (-9%); Q1 2024 $300 (-8%, holiday pull); Q2 2024 $285 (-12%). From our 2022 digital roadmap, $150 million efficiencies.

Digital direct (62% mix) $180 CAC, down 18% YoY, CPC $4.20 from $5.50 via ML bid optimization. Agents (22%) $450 improving 30% via AgentSync. Embedded (10%) $110 via Ford/GM/Toyota infotainment bundling, 25% home attach, 2-point loss shave to 62%.

Brokers $620 clawing via Vertafore APIs. P&C auto/home/renters $240 (-15%) via Guardian Bot AI at 42% conversion <60s. Life/annuities $520 (-7%), wellness hybrids halving deferrals, +18% LTV cross-sell.

U.S. $270 (-14%), Canada $290 (-10%), digital 85% per J.D. Power. Europe $340 (-8%), U.K. 20% drop via comparison sites, Germany bancassurance drag. APAC $420 (+3%) competitive, India Bajaj telematics/WeChat targeting sub-$350.

Tech: LeadGen AI on Google Cloud scores 50M prospects 92% accurately, -22% waste; dynamic DSP bids on loss forecasts amid 12% repairs per Mitchell. Payback 9 months, digital cohorts 40% faster breakeven, 35% retention via Braze.

Outlook: sub-$260 Q4 via embedded to 20%, genAI voice quoting, pet insurance adjacencies at sub-$150 CAC/40% margins. Protects 28% ROE, $100B digital P&C by 2027 per McKinsey.

Finally, our capital deployment strategy, cornerstone for shareholder value. $4.2 billion deployable capital up 12% YoY, from 92.4% P&C combined and 8.7% life embedded value growth. RBC 620% vs. 500% target, dry powder amid 15% QoQ cat drop, $250M legacy GL releases.

Framework: organic high-return investments, disciplined M&A, shareholder returns targeting mid-teens ROE.

Organic: CyberShield Elite parametric with CrowdStrike real-time intel, sub-24hr ransomware payouts amid 30% severity rise per AM Best; $450M new premiums 2024, 55-60% loss ratios (500bps better). Zenith Vitality 2.0 usage-based health with wearables/AI/gamification, 15-20% retention; SE U.S. pilots 18% conversion, $300M force-placed; Europe GDPR health 10% growth aging; APAC parametric floods $150M.

$200M Zenith Digital Labs: ML dynamic pricing -2-3pt expense; blockchain claims -40% cycles with IBM; auto telematics 12% loss edge vs. Progressive. 4-6% organic 2025, 20%+ ROIC.

Inorganic: $2.5B bolt-ons, multiples 11.5x EV/EBITDA per PwC. $1.2B InsureTech Dynamics acquisition Q4, embedded APIs for Shopify-like, 150 engineers/$180M SaaS 25% margins, $80M synergies cross-sell 5M users, 18% 3yr IRR vs. Lemonade in $100B 40% CAGR market.

$900M Pacific Heritage Life Bermuda reinsurer 1.1x EV accretive, +$500M life reserves, APAC longevity $50B LPT, from 8% to Allianz 15% share amid 7% GDP.

North America $250M Midwest Workers' Comp barbell; Europe monitoring UK motor post-Brexit.

Returns: dividend +8% to $0.65/share 2.8% yield, +$1.5B buyback ($800M YTD 15% book discount). Leverage 22%, coverage >10x. 10-12% EPS CAGR to 2027, hedging 3.5% inflation/$45B fixed 4.8% yield +60bps. ESG 30% green reins per TCFD/Munich Re.

This $4.2B balanced deployment yields superior growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the GWP growth in specialty lines, particularly cyber?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Sarah. Absolutely. Our 28.4% cyber growth reflects the ransomware surge and our ability to hike rates 12-15% while expanding via Lloyd's. Tech like ML exposure scoring has de-risked it significantly, and we're seeing strong demand across regions.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of catastrophe persistence on your business?

Michael Rivera: Good morning, Mike. We've modeled $400-600 million for Q4 cats, in line with peers, and our reinsurance caps retention effectively. Ex-cat, we're trending toward our guidance, with prior-year releases providing a buffer.

Operator: Our next question from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Thanks. On capital deployment, thoughts on the InsureTech Dynamics deal synergies?

Johnathan Hale: Lisa, great question. The $80 million annual synergies from cross-selling into their 5 million users will accrete quickly, with 18% IRR, strengthening our embedded insurance position in a high-growth market.

Operator: Our next question from David Ruiz with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz: Good morning. How are CAC trends influencing your 2025 growth outlook?

Michael Rivera: David, our declining CAC to sub-$260 supports efficient scaling, especially embedded at $110. With LTV at 4.2x, it bolsters ROE while we expand digital channels.

Operator: Our final question from Emily Foster with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Foster: Good morning. Combined ratio guidance seems aggressive—any key assumptions?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Emily. It's based on rate adequacy, telematics improvements, and expense leverage from AI. Risks like cats are covered by strong liquidity, but our Fortress strategy keeps us disciplined.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
